name: Kowaki
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only wordlists exist (Z'graggen 1975, 1980, 1-4 pp.); no grammar or phonology per Glottolog MED.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, Kowaki language page (lexicon from Z'graggen 1980)
sources.note: Wordlist only, sole source Z'graggen 1980; transcriptions carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19.
sources.note: p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' (survey-wide remark). Kowaki is not yet listed as a separate language in this 1971 volume (Mawak 28, Bepour 27 appear).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kowa1245 (references: Pick 2020; Z'graggen 1971; Campbell et al. 2022 endangerment)
sources.note: No Most Extensive Description; no grammar/phonology/sketch entries (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. PhD diss., University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 486 pp. ScholarSpace.
sources.note: pp. 31-32: stress described only for a few Northern Adelbert languages (Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan); 'available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. Section 3.6 Kowaki (pp. 126-129): consonant phonemes, TAM morphology, nasal spreading, h-epenthesis, vowel assimilation -- nothing on stress; data = Z'graggen 1980 wordlist + Z'graggen 1971 PARADISEC recording.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kowaki language' (stub; cites Ethnologue 18 and Pick 2020)
sources.note: Nothing; confirms no further literature is cited.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Introduction pp. vii-x read: transcription 'semi-phonemic', lists fluctuating sounds per language (Kowaki f~v, v~w); no mention of stress or accent anywhere; Kowaki forms (column F8) carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Kowaki (F8) listed with c. 30 speakers, one of the two smallest languages of the district.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Kowaki appears as F8 in the Tiboran family and in pronoun/lexical comparison tables only.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2022. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. In Epps, Law & Pat-El (eds.), Historical Linguistics and Endangered Languages, 215-262. Routledge.

sources.citation: Tupper, Ian. 2012. Endangered languages documentation: Pamosu (PhD/MA, La Trobe or ANU; cited by Pick 2020 as Tupper 2012: 99-102 on stress)

sources.note: NOT Kowaki: the closest well-described Tibor relative (Pamosu, pamo1252?) with an explicit stress description (final stress with closed final syllable, antepenult with open final, many exceptions). Useful only as a family-level comparandum; must not be entered as Kowaki.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. (collector). 1971. John Z'graggen's recordings, PARADISEC collection JZ2 -- Kowaki elicitation session (the 'Z'graggen 1971b' of Pick 2020)

sources.note: The only primary audio of Kowaki; the sole material from which a stress pattern could be established (by listening/instrumental analysis), since no written description exists. Pick 2020 used it for morphology but reports nothing on stress.
